blocks.text: From personal vulnerability to collective histories, ‘A Poem for Deep Thinkers’ traces the intersections of identity, memory and psychological unrest at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago.

What does it mean to navigate the complexities of Black identity in a world shaped by historical trauma and contemporary uncertainty? In ‘A Poem for Deep Thinkers ’ , acclaimed American artist Rashid Johnson returns to the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago with an expansive exhibition that examines the relationships between race, cultural memory, philosophy, and the human psyche.

Bringing together more than 70 works spanning two decades, the exhibition traces Johnson’s evolving visual language, from the black-and-white photographs of The New Negro Escapist Social and Athletic Club , informed by W. E. B. Du Bois, to his Cosmic Slops reliefs constructed from black soap and wax. His Anxious Men and Broken Men series confront the psychological pressures of contemporary existence, transforming personal unease into a broader reflection on vulnerability, alienation and collective experience.

Returning to the institution that presented his early work, Johnson invites audiences to consider how material, gesture and cultural inheritance can articulate experiences that resist easy definition. The exhibition offers a compelling encounter with an artist who continually questions what it means to exist, remember, and endure.
This exhibition will be on view at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago , USA, from 7 November 2026 to 25 April 2027.
